author: Natalie Stechyson
description: A Las Vegas court convicted Ontario man Mitchell Fairbarn of animal cruelty charges Monday for snatching a flamingo named Peachy from its habitat at the Flamingo Las Vegas Hotel and Casino last March in what prosecutors called a drunken and malicious act.
title: Canadian who stole a Las Vegas flamingo after drinking '30 to 40' beers convicted of animal cruelty
Yellowknife election: Polls closing soon as voters choose next mayor, councillors

author: Meghan Grant
description: Before he was airlifted to hospital and intubated, Sean Hiatt managed to call his mom and tell her he'd been injured in a training accident at CFB Wainwright. He was coherent at the time, according to his sister, and it gave the family hope. Now they're focused on his immediate care, and taking things 12 hours at a time.
title: 'Not out of the woods': Family rallies around soldier badly burned in CFB Wainwright fire

author: Michele McDougall
description: Leonard Foidart built a cot so he can knit comfortably while lying down. The 84-year-old from Notre-Dame-de-Lourdes, Man., lost his legs decades ago and finds it difficult to sit but loves to knit, donating more than 1,000 tuques in the last five years.
title: Man who lost legs to MS warming heads and hearts by knitting tuques on custom-made cot

author: Gregory Strong
description: The Grand Slam of Curling's competition committee plans to meet this week to discuss an unusual finish at the Co-op Invitational that sent two Canadian teams into the playoffs and led to pointed words from an American rink left outside the cutline.
title: Curling controversy: Unusual finish generates boos, ruffles feathers at Slam event

description: Gangs in Haiti opened fire on an armoured vehicle over the weekend, leaving four soldiers from El Salvador unaccounted for in the first major attack since an international gang suppression force began operations in the violence-wracked Caribbean country.
title: 4 soldiers from El Salvador missing in Haiti after attack by gangs

author: Anja Karadeglija
description: In the lawsuit filed on Oct. 6, Postmedia, Torstar, The Globe and Mail and The Canadian Press say Anthropic infringed on their copyright by using their content to develop its large language AI model, Claude.
title: Anthropic sued by major Canadian news publishers for copyright claims in Ontario court

description: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) says ‌funding shortages are forcing major cuts to its aid program in Gaza, leaving about 500,000 people without monthly food support in a territory where two-thirds of the population struggle to get enough to eat.
title: UN food program funding cuts force group to slash aid to Gazans already struggling to eat

author: Alex Nino Gheciu
description: On Friday, the bass singer Gabriel Sanchez-Ortega held up the flag at the end of Giacomo Puccini's drama about love and betrayal during political upheaval in Napoleonic Rome.
title: Calgary Opera replaces performer who unfurled Palestinian flag during Tosca bow

author: Helen Surgenor
description: 'You Can See Everything' is the movie everyone wants to talk about but no one wants spoiled. It's drawing big numbers at the box office.
title: 'You Can See Everything' sells out theatres, and people can't stop talking about it

author: Alanna Kelly
description: Marine conservation officers are searching for an injured humpback whale that passengers aboard a B.C. Ferries vessel say they felt being struck on Sunday.
title: DFO searching for injured whale struck by B.C. Ferries vessel in Howe Sound

author: Colleen Connors
description: A Port au Port West man has been sentenced to seven years in prison for shooting a snowmobiler in the head almost two years ago.
title: N.L. man sentenced to 7 years in prison for shooting snowmobiler in head

author: Christine Pagulayan
description: Apu Nahasapeemapetilon has spoken on The Simpsons for the first time since 2017, returning in Sunday's episode, "Treehouse of Horror Presents: The Revengening." The character has appeared in the background in the years since, but remained silent amid criticism that he reinforced racial stereotypes.
title: The Simpsons' Apu is back in Springfield after nearly a decade — with a new voice

description: Paris police issued an overnight curfew on Monday in two areas of the French capital in efforts to prevent further violence, after a weekend marred by France's worst rioting in years that targeted city halls, other public buildings and thousands of businesses across the country.
title: Police issue curfew in Paris after weekend rioting over cost of living, school conditions

author: Bartley Kives
description: Former Winnipeg mayor Sam Katz “violated the public trust” and former city chief administrative officer Phil Sheegl displayed “a complete lack of a moral compass” by engaging in "blatant" conflicts of interest involving the owner of the construction company awarded the contract to build the city’s police headquarters, the provincial public inquiry into the scandal-plagued project concluded.
title: Former Winnipeg mayor Sam Katz violated public trust, ex-CAO lacked moral compass, police HQ inquiry says

author: Karissa Donkin
description: The Canadian women's hockey team will take a young roster to the world championship in Denmark next month. It will be the first major tournament since the Canadians lost the Olympic final to the U.S. in February.
title: 6 players to make worlds debut as Canadian women's hockey team looks to youth

author: Benjamin Shingler, Leah Hendry
description: Some students and alumni in McGill University's law faculty have signed a petition calling for the school to allow Jeffrey George Ewert, a convicted murderer on day parole, to return to campus.
title: Petition urges McGill to allow convicted murderer on day parole back into law classes

author: Bob Becken
description: The workers are stationed at factories in Windsor and Toronto — as well as the idled Brampton assembly plant.
title: Unifor Stellantis workers vote 97% in favour of strike mandate with talks still stalled

description: Fifty-three people were killed and 200 were injured in an attack on Monday by Iran-aligned Houthi rebels on a government security forces training camp in ‌Yemen's coastal Shabwa province, according to the local authority.
title: Houthi attack on Yemeni government forces kills 53: officials

author: Baneet Braich
description: B.C.'s provincial parties are sharing their priorities for health care ahead of the Oct. 24 election, with promises ranging from more recruitment, to accelerated training for international graduates, to new health centres.
title: What health-care promises have B.C. parties made ahead of the provincial election?

description: Israeli police said they arrested 10 people on Monday in connection with a wave of settler violence that included attacks on a foreign journalist and European diplomats in the occupied West Bank over the weekend.
title: Israel arrests 10 people after West Bank settler attacks on diplomats, journalist

description: AI data centres have become a hot-button political issue the world over, and in British Columbia it's no different.
title: Where do B.C.'s parties stand on the future of AI data centres?

author: Jeff Lagerquist
description: Statistics Canada says the pace of inflation picked up in September, as prices for gasoline climbed at a faster rate than in August.
title: Inflation rises to 3.1%, as fuel prices push higher: StatsCan

description: Russia launched new attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure using ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday, adding that Kyiv again received no early warning of the attack from partner countries that previously shared their intelligence.
title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine given no early warning from allies as Russia strikes energy targets

description: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines was in a critical ‌condition on Monday after being deliberately struck by a car outside her office in Wangaratta, police and Prime ​Minister Anthony Albanese said.
title: Australian MP Helen Haines in critical condition after deliberate vehicle attack, prime minister says

description: With less than six months to go, the territory is preparing to transfer some federal jobs to the Nunavut government, create a new department responsible for lands and resources and pass a series of legislative changes that implement devolution.
title: Q&A | Nunavut’s devolution is 6 months away. Here’s what the premier says to expect

author: Celina Aalders
description: Nova Scotia does not have a provincewide policy explicitly stating how AI should be used in the classroom. The provincial government says it’s up to regional centres for education to make their own rules about the technology. Parents and educators are calling for more consistency, and say guardrails are needed.
title: Inconsistent guidelines for AI use in N.S. classrooms fuel calls for provincewide policy

author: Talia Ricci
description: If you've been looking to buy a home in Ontario, you may have seen a few listings where the furniture doesn't look quite right. That's because many of them are being staged virtually, using AI. Experts say there are benefits and drawbacks of the tool.
title: Rising use of AI-staged real estate photos raises questions about misleading homebuyers

description: This high school baseball team hasn't won a game in six years. But the Dartmouth High Spartans say their losing streak gives everyone a chance to play. The CBC's Meig Campbell went to meet the team with the winning spirit.
title: This baseball team has lost every game for 6 years. But they feel like winners

author: Erica Johnson, Ana Komnenic
description: Every year, Canadians lose hundreds of millions to bank fraud — and are often left footing the bill. Now, customers of TD, Royal Bank, Scotiabank, CIBC and the Bank of Montreal are calling on Ottawa to hold banks more liable for fraud losses.
title: Bank fraud victims want Ottawa to make big banks pay more

author: Murray Brewster
description: NATO's supreme commander of transformation says the West's greatest vulnerability may not be a shortage of weapons, but the time it takes to build them — and the speed at which its adversaries are learning to fight.
title: NATO's race against time: Senior commander warns alliance must adapt faster to deter Russia
